content: Show your child affection and express your love openly. Pay attention to your child’s interests and respond to them thoughtfully. Offer praise when your child makes an effort to learn new skills. From birth, your baby begins to learn. Encourage play by providing opportunities for your baby to see, hear, move their arms and legs freely, and touch you. Gently soothe, stroke, and hold your baby, as skin-to-skin contact is highly beneficial. Engage in communication by looking into your baby’s eyes and talking to them, especially during breastfeeding, which is an ideal time for bonding. Facilitate play by offering ways for your child to see, hear, feel, and move freely. Slowly move colorful objects for your baby to see and reach for. Examples of toys include a shaker rattle or a large ring on a string. Smile and laugh with your child, and talk to them regularly. Provide clean, safe household items for your child to handle, bang, and drop, such as containers with lids or a metal pot and spoon. Respond to your child’s sounds and interests to foster communication. Encourage play by hiding your child’s favorite toy under a cloth or box and seeing if they can find it. Play games like peek-a-boo to stimulate their curiosity. Communicate by naming objects and people for your child to learn. Offer your child items to stack, place into containers, and remove, such as nesting and stacking objects or containers with clothespins. Ask your child simple questions and respond to their attempts to talk. Help your child count, name, and compare objects. Create simple toys, such as items of different colors and shapes for sorting, or provide tools like a chalkboard, stick, or puzzle. Encourage your child to talk and answer their questions. Teach them stories, songs, and games, and discuss pictures or books to enhance their learning and communication skills.
